items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The 12th of November I recorded under my own name with Stephane Grappelli, Joseph Reinhardt on guitar...

ctx.x: "Hang Over Blues" was just a name that I decided on and not because I had a hangover. Another number was recorded but never issued. It was "Sometimes I'm Happy". I never found out why it was never issued and have no idea what it really sounded like. This Combelle record was recorded the 4th of October 1937.

The 18th of October Willie Lewis and his orchestra recorded six numbers with the full band. The 12th of November I recorded under my own name with Stephane Grappelli, Joseph Reinhardt on guitar, Wilson Meyers and Ted Fields, drums. Grappelli surprised me by playing piano on some of the numbers. Whenever Hugues Panassie asked me to record I seldom asked who the other musicians would be unless I was asked to choose them. And that was the reason I was surprised when I arrived at the studio and I knew the instruments…

November the 19th I recorded "Bill Coleman Blues" accompanied only by Django on guitar which was another first for Hugues Panassie because it was his idea to record just the two of us for one number and it was the first time a trumpet and guitar had been recorded on a jazz record. The other five numbers recorded on that date had Christian Wagner clarinet and alto, "Big Boy" Godie tenor and clarinet, Emil Stern, piano, Lucien Simoens, bass, and Jerry Mengo drums.
